name: web
// targets: to see all targets run: nx show project web --web

build.// env: Nx injects the workspace-root and project-root `.env` files into every target's environment. Both carry NODE_ENV=development (they are dev env files — see doc/decision/0009-*), which would otherwise leak into `next build` and produce a mixed development/production React resolution. Pin it here; see doc/decision/0028-*.

start.// env: The same `.env` injection the build target guards against reaches `next start` too, and Next.js says so out loud: `⚠ You are using a non-standard "NODE_ENV" value in your environment.` Serving a production build under NODE_ENV=development is exactly the mixed resolution doc/decision/0028-* is about — and `web:start` is what the e2e suite runs (doc/decision/0187-*), so without this pin the suite's claim to exercise the app production runs is only half true.

dev.// port: The same `.env` injection the build target guards against also carries PORT=3000 — the API's port (`.env`, §API). `next dev` reads PORT when no `--port` is given, so the inferred `next dev` bound 3000 and collided with `api:serve` (EADDRINUSE). The flag wins over the environment variable, which is why the port is spelled here rather than removed from `.env`. 4200 is not a preference either: `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` and the Okta redirect URI registered with the mock OIDC server both name http://localhost:4200.
